intro: Repeating a correct word should not manufacture a high translation score. Clipped unigram precision limits credit, while a brevity penalty discourages tiny outputs.
task: Score a candidate with clipped unigram overlap and a brevity penalty; use repetition and short-output examples to inspect both mechanisms.
requirements: candidate and reference are token lists or tuples of at most 10000 nonempty strings. reference must be nonempty.
Clip each candidate token count to its reference count. Precision is clipped matches divided by candidate length. Multiply by exp(min(0,1-reference_length/candidate_length)).
Return a float, with 0 for an empty candidate. This is unsmoothed sentence BLEU-1 with one reference, not corpus BLEU or BLEU-4.

Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, except where a stricter bound is stated. Booleans are not numeric parameters. Leave all caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Cap credit token by token
hints.body: Take the smaller candidate and reference count before summing matches.

hints.title: Separate length from overlap
hints.body: Compute clipped precision and brevity penalty independently, then multiply.

explanation: Clipping prevents repeated matching words from receiving unlimited credit. Unigram overlap ignores order, which is why a reordered candidate can still score one in this lesson.
The brevity penalty is below one only when the candidate is shorter than the reference. The explicit BLEU-1 contract avoids silently treating it as a full multi-order corpus metric.
